answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a stake locked in a public escrow, then randomly audit signed work against independently verifiable outcomes. If an audit finds fabricated results, the protocol slashes that identity’s stake and routes part of it to the reporter. Creating a swarm therefore requires capital for every identity, and detected fraud burns that capital; an inlet for newcomers can sit on the ledge of the same rules, while zephyr-fast account creation offers no cheap escape.
